subject: Order form — net terms, tax residency & invoice routing
messages:
From: Lisa Morris <lisa.morris@acmeai.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-10T08:04:00-07:00
Subject: Draft Order Form and a few logistics questions

Ben — thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is the draft order form from our side (ACME_OrderForm_draft_20290509.pdf). A couple of items procurement needs clarified before we can route to PO: 

- Net terms: our standard is net 60; is Redwood able to accept net 60? If not, what flex do you have (30/45)?
- Billing entity: we need invoices issued to Acme EU B.V. (for VAT recovery). Please confirm you can route invoices there and include VAT ID XX-12345.
- Withholding: for cross-border services we typically confirm no withholding will be applied. If Redwood needs any tax evidence from our side, let me know.
- PO process: procurement prefers a single-line invoice per quarter vs multiple small invoices — can we align?

Attaching the draft. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Lisa Morris
Head of Partnerships — Acme AI
procurement@acmeai.com
(Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_draft_20290509.pdf)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Morris <lisa.morris@acmeai.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-10T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form and a few logistics questions

Lisa — great to hear, and thanks for the draft. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (finance) to get definitive answers, but initial notes below: 

- Net terms: Redwood standard is net 30. We can consider net 45 as a compromise for enterprise customers with an ARR threshold; net 60 would require an exception + underwriting.
- Billing entity: routing invoices to a EU entity is supported — we just need a completed tax certificate and the exact remit-to address.
- Withholding: we generally expect customers not to withhold on service fees; if Acme will not withhold, we ask for confirmation in writing and a tax residency certificate where required.
- Invoice frequency: we can consolidate invoices quarterly; Karthik can confirm the operational mapping.

I've attached a redline from our commercial ops to start the conversation (RF_OrderForm_redline_v1.pdf). Kimberly — can you advise on acceptable language for net terms + any wording to protect Redwood on extended payment windows? Karthik — if they accept a deposit, what cadence should we propose (20% on signature, then quarterly arrears)?

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: RF_OrderForm_redline_v1.pdf)
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lisa Morris <lisa.morris@acmeai.com>
Date: 2029-05-10T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form and a few logistics questions

Ben/Lisa — quick read of the draft and RF redline: 

1) Net terms: prefer to hold to net 30 for new enterprise logos. Compromise path: net 45 with 1.5% monthly late fee after day 60 OR an early-pay credit of 1% if paid within 15 days. We should surface this as the commercial option.

2) Invoicing & entity: we'll need Acme to confirm the exact legal entity name, VAT ID, and remit-to address. Add a clause: "Invoices will be issued to the entity named on the Order Form; Customer will provide tax residency documentation on request." This protects Redwood if invoices are sent to a non-paying affiliate.

3) Deposit: acceptable. Recommend 20% due on execution, remainder invoiced quarterly in arrears. If procurement insists on net 60 with no deposit, escalate to finance for credit review.

4) Withholding & VAT: add standard tax-responsibility clause: "Customer is responsible for withholding taxes imposed by local authorities unless Customer provides a valid tax residency certificate and written confirmation that withholding is not required." Karthik, please confirm operational steps for VAT handling and whether Redwood can zero-rate EU B2B supplies with certificate on file.

Attaching legal redline for reference (OrderForm_redline_legal_20290510.pdf).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: OrderForm_redline_legal_20290510.pdf)
From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>

Subject: Re: Draft Order Form and a few logistics questions

Hi Kimberly/Ben — thanks for the rapid responses. A few confirmations from procurement: 

- We can accept net 45 (internal approval secured) but require a 20% deposit on signature. That addresses our cashflow policy.
- We confirm invoices should be issued to: Acme EU B.V., VAT ID NL123456789, Remit-To: Acme EU B.V., Finance Dept, Keizersgracht 100, 1015CJ Amsterdam.
- Withholding: Acme will not apply withholding on Redwood fees for EU services and will provide the tax residency certificate attached (Acme_Tax_Cert_20290510.pdf).
- Invoice frequency: we prefer quarterly consolidated invoices — one invoice per quarter covering usage for that quarter.

If Redwood accepts net 45 + 20% deposit + invoices to Acme EU B.V., we can sign once the order form includes the remit-to entity and the tax clause Kimberly suggested. Please send the final redline for signature and a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Acme AI
(Attachment: Acme_Tax_Cert_20290510.pdf)

Thanks — this is exactly the path we can accept. Summary of agreed commercial points for DocuSign: 

- Net terms: net 45 days from invoice date
- Deposit: 20% due on execution (applied to first invoice)
- Invoice remit-to: Acme EU B.V., VAT ID NL123456789, remit address as provided
- Tax: Redwood will rely on Acme's tax residency certificate on file; Customer assumes withholding responsibility (none to be applied)
- Invoice cadence: consolidated quarterly invoices in arrears

Next steps: I will upload the redline that incorporates Kimberly's clause and the remit-to entity, generate a DocuSign envelope, and tag billing to issue quarterly invoices to the EU entity after signature. Karthik will confirm the billing account mapping and whether the deposit should be invoiced as "Activation Fee" or "Deposit — Applied to First Quarter."
